1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the orchestrator for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (one of four) and run one round-trip end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
12	read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
17	
18	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
19	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
20	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (CSR write, PC, instruction count, or SimPoint phase)
21	hands control between them. One run is three legs:
22	
23	```
24	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim  -- same files -->  QEMU2
25	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)         (fast)
26	```
27	
28	The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
29	leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
30	mode".
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 0.5 Quick start with `./hsim`
35	
36	`./hsim` is the canonical end-user entry point. It wraps the
37	developer-grade scripts documented in Sections 1-5 (`setup.sh`,
38	`tests/e2e.sh`, `scripts/run_e2e.sh`) behind four subcommands.
39	
40	Four-command worked example - cold checkout to passing suite:
41	
42	```sh
43	./hsim build                                            # qemu, vsim, plugin, simpoint, fixtures
44	./hsim list fixtures                                    # discover available fixtures
45	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf --mode csr     # one CSR-mode round-trip

498	### 4.1 CSR mode - the default (kernel)
499	
500	Goal: run a vector fixture through QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 using the
501	two `csrwi 0x7C0, *` markers that the fixture already contains.
502

513	`hsim run --mode csr` is a thin Python wrapper around the generic
514	`tests/e2e.sh` harness. Inside, the three legs are:
515	
516	```
517	1) QEMU1 with -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE
518	        -> drain at csrwi 0x7C0,0   -> exit 200
519	2) sim_ax45mpv_premium $ELF \
520	        --resume-from-qemu $STATE --handoff-out $STATE_V \
521	        --shared-mem-path $SHM --shared-mem-size 128MB
522	        -> ROI runs in vsim, drains at csrwi 0x7C0,1   -> exit 200
523	3) python3 -m orchestrator.main qemu-resume \
524	        --state $STATE_V --mmap $SHM --size 128MB
525	        -> spawns QEMU2, restores state via gdbstub, continues,
526	           exits 0 via semihosting (the run tail).
527	```
528	
529	Try a different fixture:
530	
531	```sh
532	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.elf --mode csr
533	```
534	
535	### 4.2 PC mode - markerless workload, explicit boundary PCs
536	
537	Same plumbing as CSR mode, but the binary carries **no** trigger markers.
538	The user picks the switch PCs explicitly via `--pc-start` and `--pc-end`,
539	each a symbol name or `0x` address. Both args are required for `--mode pc`.
540	
541	```sh
542	# resolve the boundary PCs once (cheap, host-side; needs HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
543	ELF=tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf
544	START=vmatmul_kernel
545	END=$(${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump -d "$ELF" \
546	        | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
547	        | tr -d ':')
548	
549	./hsim run "$ELF" --mode pc --pc-start "$START" --pc-end "$END"
550	```
551	
552	`rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` is the **markerless twin** of the GEMM fixture,
553	built `-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS` from the same source as the marked
554	`rt_c_v_matmul`. Both triggers are one-shot (QEMU plugin `exit(200)` on
555	first match; vsim drains on first match), so the measured window is
556	**exactly one full `vmatmul_kernel` call** (16 outer rows + inner k-loop
557	+ vse32 stores). The cycle count should land near CSR mode's ~22808.
558	
559	The mechanism is fully general - pc mode can target **any** symbol or raw
560	address. Under `tests/e2e.sh` the same knobs are the `ROI_START` /
561	`ROI_END` env vars; `hsim run --mode pc` forwards `--pc-start` / `--pc-end`
562	into those env vars for you.
563	
564	To see what `hsim run --mode pc` passes under the hood:
565	
566	```sh
567	# Resolve the boundaries (objdump-based; pick any two PCs in the ELF):
568	OBJDUMP=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
569	NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm
570	ROI_START=$("$NM" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
571	              | awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print "0x"$1}')
572	ROI_END=$("$OBJDUMP" -d tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
573	              | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
574	              | tr -d ':')
575	echo "enter=$ROI_START  exit=$ROI_END"   # e.g. 0x10021c / 0x1002cc
576	
577	# QEMU1 leg
578	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
579	  -object memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=/dev/shm/share,size=134217728 \
580	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
581	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
582	  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
583	  -bios tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
584	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=/tmp/q1.bin,enter_pc=$ROI_START"
585	
586	# vsim leg
587	"$VSIM_BIN" tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
588	  --resume-from-qemu /tmp/q1.bin \
589	  --handoff-out /tmp/v.bin \
590	  --shared-mem-path /dev/shm/share \
591	  --shared-mem-size 134217728 \
592	  --hybrid-exit-pc "$ROI_END"
593	
594	# QEMU2 leg (orchestrator restores state via gdbstub, runs to completion)
595	PYTHONPATH=tools python3 -m orchestrator.main qemu-resume \
596	  --state /tmp/v.bin \
597	  --mmap /dev/shm/share \
598	  --size 134217728
599	```

607	a **single boundary** on each side: QEMU fast-forwards `--qemu-icount` insns,
608	vsim measures `--vsim-icount` insns and drains. The cycle figure (window

611	to exclude the first K cold-cache insns from the reported figure.
612
